reading_flow.text: Lab-based activity 5.1: Laboratory works. The objectives are to observe and identify three cell types. The materials required are microscopes, specimens of cardiac, skeletal, and smooth muscles, and knives. The methods are to: prepare a specimen for all three muscle types, set a wet mounting of each specimen, observe the samples under the microscope, and write a lab report. The assessments are: what are the differences among the three types of muscles, draw a diagram of each type of muscle, and explain the relationships between the structures and functions of muscles.

reading_flow.text: 5.1.2. Mechanism of actions of skeletal muscles
What are mechanisms of action? They are the process of activating muscle cells to generate tension or contract for movements, where cells work together to generate muscle contractions and movement.

Skeletal muscles are bundles of muscle fibers composed of single large cells formed by the fusion of many individual cells during development. Most of the cytoplasm in these cells consists of myofibrils, which are cylindrical bundles containing two types of filaments: thick filaments made of myosin and thin filaments made of actin. Each of these is organized as a chain of contractile units called sarcomeres.

audio_hyperlinks.explanation: Thread-like structures in muscle cells that contain the contractile filaments.
The basic functional unit of a muscle fiber that shortens during contraction.

reading_flow.text: Actin and myosin are proteins found in every type of muscle tissue. The thick myosin filaments and thin actin filaments work together to generate muscle contractions. Myosin acts as a molecular motor, converting chemical energy released from ATP into mechanical energy used to pull the actin filaments, causing the muscle fibers to contract. Actin filaments and myosin together are responsible for many types of cell movements, with muscle contraction being the most noticeable form.
